testId: testim-migrated/tests/webstore/pdp/verify-add-to-cart-functionality-on-pdp.spec.ts > Webstore - PDP > verify add to cart functionality on pdp

scenario.summary: Guest searches the webstore for a bundle product by SKU, opens its PDP, checks breadcrumb and name, adds it to the cart (quantity 1), then adds each Frequently Bought Together product (2) and each You May Also Like product (3) from the PDP, checking the cart count after every add and a total of 6.
steps: Open the webstore as a guest (empty storageState).
Search the product SKU, assert 'Showing 1 of 1 Results', open the result and check the product image.
Assert breadcrumb Home/<category path>/<product name> and the product heading.
Assert the 'Add to Cart' button, add the product to the cart; the flyout shows 'Add to Cart', SKU and Qty 1; cart count 1.
For each Frequently Bought Together product: assert its heading, add it to the cart, cart count +1.
For each You May Also Like product: assert its heading, add it to the cart, cart count +1.
Assert the total cart count equals expectedCartCount (6).
stateChanges: Guest cart receives the main product and its 5 related products (session cart only; no order placed).
assertions: Search shows 'Showing 1 of 1 Results' and the product image is visible.
Breadcrumb equals Home/<category path>/<product name>; heading equals the product name.
Add to Cart button and flyout label read 'Add to Cart'; cart notification contains 'SKU: <sku>' and 'Qty: 1'.
Each related product heading shows its name; cart count increases by one per add and ends at 6.
evidence: Title 'verify add to cart functionality on pdp' and step labels 1) to 6) match the flow; spec comment says 'open the bundle PDP'.

GAP: the test needs a product that has 2 Frequently Bought Together and 3 You May Also Like associated products (and its category path for the breadcrumb). No vocabulary key covers related-product associations, and PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IN_STOCK returns no category path or related products. If the resolver falls back from the recorded bundle, the related-product values no longer belong to it.
Related products, category path and expectedCartCount are kept as values of the product need (alias product) only because no key supplies them; they must come from a key once one exists.
migrate: productCategory and the related-product values map to no output of PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IN_STOCK, and expectedCartCount (6) is derived from the number of related products in the data.
No data value appears in the spec code; the spec reads the JSON through loadData.
Remap 2026-11-03: productSKU -> product.sku, productName -> product.name, productCategory (breadcrumb 'Tools / Power Tools') -> product.categoryPath (new output, ' / '-joined path).

Remap 2026-11-03: New needs frequentlyBought / youMayAlsoLike -> PRODUCT_LINKED_PRODUCTS {product @product.productId, linkType FrequentlyBought | YouMayAlsoLike, store, minLinked 2 | 3 (the cards the test walks through)}: the related products now come from the resolved product's own links (first three in PDP display order), so they stay consistent when the resolver falls back from the recorded product. Supersedes the GAP / missing-key lines on related products.

Remap 2026-11-03: frequentlyBoughtProducts.0..1 and youMayAlsoLike.0..2 names / SKUs -> frequentlyBought / youMayAlsoLike linkedNName / linkedNSku. PRODUCT_LINKED_PRODUCTS does not require the linked products to be in stock (linkedNQuantity is their stock on the store); the test adds each one to the cart.
Remap 2026-11-03: expectedCartCount (6) stays config: it is 1 + the cards added (2 + 3, the minLinked values); the spec may compute it.
